messages.content: Predict this participant’s allocation. You decide how to divide EUR 10 between yourself and another participant. You may keep an amount from EUR 0 to EUR 10; the rest is given to the other participant. One of the experiment’s decisions is randomly selected for payment. If this dictator decision is selected, participants are randomly paired and assigned dictator or receiver roles; the chosen dictator’s allocation determines the pair’s payment. A separate EUR 4 show-up fee is paid. Answer only the number of euros you choose to keep, without explanation.
You are a 22-year-old male economics student at the University of Kiel. Make your allocation of EUR 10: how many euros do you keep for yourself?

Predict this participant’s portfolio allocation. Allocate a fresh budget of 100 ECU between options A and B. Both entries must be whole numbers from 0 to 100 and sum to 100; any such split is allowed. Four states have equal probability, 25% each. The table lists percentages of the amount invested in the corresponding option, in state order 1, 2, 3, 4. Direct returns go to you. A has no pool contribution. A B-pool return goes into a common pool, not directly to you in full. If a social investment problem is paid, four randomly grouped participants face the same selected problem and the same state for both options and for all four people. All four pool contributions are added and divided equally among all four, including you, regardless of their own investments. Your return is your direct return from A plus your direct return from B plus one quarter of the group pool. Negative rates produce a negative direct return. In an individual problem both options pay only you and there is no common pool. Splitting investments does not give independent state draws or diversify state risk. One of the experiment’s decisions is selected randomly for payment, with the state drawn only after decisions. The 100 ECU is an allocation budget; payment is based on the selected realized returns. A separate EUR 4 show-up fee is paid. Decisions have no time limit. Once confirmed a choice cannot be revised; no decision or outcome feedback is given during the task. Answer only a JSON object with the integer ECU amounts, for example {"A_ECU":40,"B_ECU":60}.
